About me

A student by day,
a shipper by night.

I'm Muhammad Tayyab Imran, a third-semester BS Software Engineering student at The University of Faisalabad (session 2025–2029), holding a 3.72 CGPA. I come from Chak 96 RB, a small village between Jaranwala and Shahkot in Punjab — most people know the town, so "from Shahkot" is what I say.

I learn by building things people can actually use. My Blood Donation Management System started as a Kotlin + SQLite Android app and grew, release by release, into a signed, self-updating product backed by Supabase Auth and row-level security. My NeuralChat web app is live in production, hardened through five review rounds — security fixes, rate limiting, lazy loading and all.

This semester I'm deep into Data Structures, Theory of Automata, Software Engineering and Calculus — and somewhere between lectures and GitHub Actions runs, I still find time to finish DigiSkills certifications in Freelancing and AI with Python.

Selected work

Things I've actually shipped.

Not tutorial clones — real releases with version numbers, signing keys, changelogs and users, from Android and the web to WhatsApp bots and a music player. Move your cursor over a card; they lean in.

Android · v1.4 released

Blood Donation Management System

Kotlin · SQLite · Supabase — github release, signed APK

A complete donor-management app built for my university project and released like a real product: four versions in, with an in-app updater that pulls new signed builds straight from GitHub Releases.

  • Real accounts — email sign-up & login via Supabase Auth, token-based sync
  • Protected data — row-level security: only signed-in users read or write
  • Donor logic — eligibility checks (age 18–65, ≥50 kg, 90-day gap), 8-group stock, request matching
  • Offline-first — local SQLite keeps working with no connection
KotlinAndroidSQLite Supabase AuthPostgRESTGitHub Actions

Web · Live in production

NeuralChat

TypeScript · React — live at neuralchat.live

An AI chat web app, live on its own domain and deployed through Vercel. It went through five structured review rounds before I called it done — every round a report, a diff, and fixes verified by a full green test run.

  • Live & public — deployed at neuralchat.live with auto-deploy on push
  • Security pass — markdown XSS hole closed, image MIME mismatch fixed
  • Abuse protection — per-IP rate limiting on the search API
  • Performance — lazy loading and store-ordering fixes across the chat UI
TypeScriptReactVercel Gemini APIREST
Visit neuralchat.live ↗ GitHub profile ↗
WhatsApp bot · v2.0.0

Optimus Bot

JavaScript · Node.js · Baileys — WhatsApp automation

A full-featured WhatsApp bot for group management, AI chat, media tools and fun — multi-device with pairing-code login, and a test suite that passes 363 out of 363.

  • Group management — anti-link, anti-badword, warnings, bans, mute, kick, promote & demote
  • AI built in — Groq chat with Gemini fallback, image generation and voice-note transcription
  • Media & stickers — downloads from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and more, plus sticker maker
  • Everyday tools — reminders, scheduled messages, polls, games like Tic-Tac-Toe and trivia
JavaScriptNode.jsBaileys GroqGeminiWhatsApp
View on GitHub ↗
Android · Music player

NovaMusic

Kotlin · Jetpack Compose · Material 3 — YouTube Music client

An Android YouTube Music client with a modern Material 3 interface, developed from the OpenTune / InnerTune open-source lineage and rebranded under its own identity, package and release channel.

  • Real offline downloads — songs saved as actual playable files in Music/NovaMusic, not a hidden cache
  • Background-proof — downloads run through WorkManager with live per-song progress
  • Own update channel — the in-app updater checks NovaMusic's own GitHub Releases
  • Signed releases — CI-published APKs, with releases up to v2.0.15
KotlinJetpack ComposeMedia3 / ExoPlayer RoomHiltWorkManager

The lab

Don't just read about the app. Play with it.

This is the compatibility engine from the Blood Donation app, running right here. Pick a blood group and a direction — the matches light up.

red-cell compatibility · all 8 groups
Pick a blood group above to see who it matches.

Fun fact from the data: O− is the universal donor and AB+ the universal recipient — which is exactly why the app flags O− donors first when a request comes in.
